title: Ration Card 2026: Status Check, e-KYC & Free Ration Rules
meta_description: Check ration card status on nfsa.gov.in, complete mandatory e-KYC, and claim free grain under PMGKAY till December 2028. ONORC and member updates covered.

hero.one_liner: Check your ration card status, apply for a new card, or update member details - all online through your state's food department portal

sections.title: 📌 Two Things That Decide Your Ration in 2026 (Verified August 2026)
sections.content:
Free grain under PMGKAY runs till 31 December 2028. NFSA cardholders pay nothing: PHH gets 5 kg per person per month, AAY gets 35 kg per family.

But e-KYC is now mandatory for every member listed on the card, not just the head. Deadlines are set state by state, and members who miss it get their grain paused until it is done.

sections.heading: What a Ration Card Actually Gets You Now
content: A ration card is issued by your state food department and entitles your family to foodgrain from a Fair Price Shop under the National Food Security Act. NFSA covers about 75% of rural and 50% of urban India, roughly 81 crore people.

The old picture of paying ₹2 per kg for wheat and ₹3 for rice is out of date. Since January 2024 the Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana has made NFSA grain free, and the Cabinet has extended that till December 2028.

The card does more than food. It is accepted as address proof, it is the only document listing every family member with relationships, and it feeds eligibility for PM-JAY, PM Awas, RTE school quota and many state schemes.
Applications are free in most states. What costs people their entitlement is not the fee, it is unfinished e-KYC and outdated member lists.

win.name: FAIR PRICE SHOP
win.sub: Fingerprint on the dealer's ePoS machine, free, works for every member who can reach the shop

others.name: MERA eKYC APP

others.name: STATE PDS PORTAL

sections.heading: e-KYC Deadlines and What Happens If You Miss
content: There is no single national deadline. Each state runs its own verification drive with its own cutoff, which is why WhatsApp forwards about dates are usually wrong for your state.

Assam's food department set 31 July 2026 for its drive, Maharashtra worked to 30 June 2026, and several large states ran deadlines earlier in the year. The only date that matters is your state's, available at your ration shop or on your state food portal.
Missing it does not usually cancel the card. What happens is the unverified member is flagged unauthenticated and their share of grain is paused until e-KYC is done.

The purpose of the drive is removing duplicate and ghost names so genuine families get their full quota. Completing it late still restores the member, so a missed deadline is a delay, not a permanent loss.

sections.heading: How to Check Ration Card Status Online

steps.title: Open nfsa.gov.in
steps.description: The national portal carries links for all states. Look for Ration Cards, then Ration Card Details on State Portals.

steps.title: Select state and district
steps.description: Choosing your state redirects you to that state's food department system, since the underlying data sits with the state.

steps.title: Search by card number or Aadhaar
steps.description: Enter the ration card number if you have it. If not, any family member's Aadhaar works, because all cards are Aadhaar-seeded.

steps.title: Read what the record shows
steps.description: You get the member list, category, monthly entitlement, assigned Fair Price Shop, and recent transactions. Check that every member appears and shows verified.

sections.heading: Why e-KYC Suddenly Became Everyone's Problem
content: Ration lists were built over decades and carry names that no longer belong there: people who died, daughters who married into other families, workers who moved and got a second card elsewhere.
Aadhaar-based e-KYC is the government's method for cleaning that up, because a fingerprint or face scan proves a real person is behind each name. Every deletion frees grain for genuine households.

The catch for honest families is that the burden falls on them too. A member who never visits the shop, like a student living in another city or an elderly parent, is exactly the profile that gets flagged.
That is why the check is worth doing proactively rather than discovering the problem when the month's grain comes up short.

sections.heading: 🗂️ Card Types, Colours and What Each Gets
rows: Poorest households identified by government survey, often elderly, widows, disabled, destitute
Families meeting state NFSA criteria, the largest group
Households above the state's NFSA line

sections.heading: Card Colours Change by State, Entitlement Does Not
content: People often ask which colour card is best, but colour coding is a state convention rather than a national rule. Yellow, pink, saffron, blue and white mean different things in different states.
What actually decides your grain is the category recorded in the system: AAY, PHH, or non-NFSA. Read the category printed on the card rather than judging by colour.
AAY cards cannot be applied for directly. Government identifies AAY households through survey data, and families are moved into that category by the food department.
Some states add their own extras on top of the central entitlement, such as additional free rice or subsidised pulses. Those extras stop at the state border, which matters when you use ONORC.

If you believe your household qualifies for a better category, the route is a category change application at the block food office with income and asset proof. Approval depends on the state's current NFSA quota, so it can take a while.

sections.heading: How to Apply for a New Ration Card
content: Applications run through your state's food portal: fcs.up.gov.in for UP, epds.bihar.gov.in for Bihar, mahafood.gov.in for Maharashtra, food.rajasthan.gov.in for Rajasthan, tnpds.gov.in for Tamil Nadu, nfs.delhi.gov.in for Delhi.

Fill the head of family details and then every member with name, age, relationship and Aadhaar. Attach address proof, an income declaration where the state asks for it, and a passport photo of the head.
Offline works identically: the Block or Taluka food office accepts the printed form with photocopies attached. A food inspector then verifies your residence and family composition.
Processing typically runs 15 to 30 days, with some states slower. You get a reference number for tracking, and the card is issued digitally in states that have moved to e-ration cards.

sections.heading: Documents Checklist
qualify: Aadhaar of every family member to be listed
Address proof: electricity bill, rent agreement, gas bill, or voter ID
Income declaration or certificate where your state requires it
Passport photo of the head of family
Bank passbook copy in states that ask for it
disqualify: A family already holding a ration card in any other state
Members already listed on a different family's card
Households above the state's NFSA income or asset criteria
Applications where member names do not match Aadhaar spelling

sections.heading: 🗓️ From Application to First Collection

items.event: Apply online or at the block office
items.desc: Submit the family details with Aadhaar for every member and address proof. Note the reference number for tracking.
A food inspector confirms your residence and family composition. Keep original documents at hand for that visit.
Most states issue within 15 to 30 days, increasingly as a digital e-ration card downloadable from the portal or DigiLocker.
Fingerprint at the shop or face scan on the Mera eKYC app. Grain does not flow for members who stay unauthenticated.

sections.heading: Adding, Removing and Correcting Members
content: Add a member through the state portal's Add Member option with their Aadhaar, date of birth and relationship. For a newborn, the birth certificate works and Aadhaar can be linked later.

Remove a member on death, marriage into another family, or permanent migration, attaching the death certificate or marriage proof. Leaving a departed member on the card is treated as a false claim during verification drives.
For PHH cards the grain is per person, so both actions change your monthly quantity. Adding a newborn adds 5 kg a month once approved.
Corrections to name spelling, age or Aadhaar number matter more than they look. A name that does not match Aadhaar is the single most common cause of biometric failure at the shop.
Family splits after partition are handled through a card split application at the block office, needing separate residence proof and consent from the existing head.
After any change, re-check the record a week later rather than assuming approval went through. Portals sometimes show the application as complete while the member list stays unchanged.

sections.heading: 🛠️ Common Problems and What Fixes Them
rows: Wrong number, or card issued very recently
Recheck the number, wait a week for new cards, or ask your FPS dealer to look it up
e-KYC not completed for that person
Fingerprint at the shop, or face authentication on the Mera eKYC app
Name mismatch with Aadhaar, or worn fingerprints
Correct the spelling on the portal; ask for iris or face authentication as the fallback
A member was removed, or e-KYC pending for someone
Check the member list on the portal and complete any pending verification
Long non-collection, duplicate found, or verification failure
Ask the food office for the reason in writing, then apply for restoration with proof
Illegal: PMGKAY grain is free for NFSA cardholders
Call 1967 or your state helpline, and file on nfsa.gov.in grievance

sections.heading: When the Machine Refuses Your Fingerprint
content: Biometric failure is common among farm and construction workers whose fingerprints wear down, and among the elderly. It is not a reason to be sent home empty-handed.
Ask the dealer to try iris scanning or face authentication, both supported on current ePoS devices. Most refusals are dealers avoiding the extra step, not a system limitation.

The other frequent cause is a spelling mismatch between the card and Aadhaar, which blocks matching regardless of how clean the fingerprint is. Correct it on the state portal with the Aadhaar copy attached.
If a shop repeatedly turns you away, note the date and dealer name, then call 1967. Denial of entitlement to an authenticated cardholder is exactly what the helpline exists for.

sections.heading: Mera Ration 2.0: The App Worth Installing
content: Mera Ration 2.0 is the government's own app for cardholders, available on Play Store and App Store. It shows your digital ration card, member list, monthly entitlement and collection history.
For migrants it is the practical tool: it locates nearby Fair Price Shops in whichever city you are in and confirms your ONORC eligibility before you walk there.
Several states now let you download the e-ration card from the app or DigiLocker, with the printed card being phased out. The digital card with QR code is accepted at the shop.
The related Mera eKYC app handles face-based verification from home, which is the easiest route for members who cannot reach the shop.

sections.heading: ONORC: Using Your Card in Another State
content: One Nation One Ration Card lets you collect your entitlement at any Fair Price Shop in India using your existing home-state card. A Bihar family working in Mumbai draws its grain at a Mumbai shop.
The mechanism is Aadhaar biometric authentication on the shop's ePoS device, which checks your entitlement against the central database in seconds. No transfer application, no new card.
The limitation worth knowing: ONORC carries your central NFSA entitlement, not state-specific extras. Additional grain or items given by your home state stay behind when you collect elsewhere.

If a dealer claims ONORC does not work at their shop, it is almost always reluctance rather than a technical block. Ask them to run the portability option on the ePoS machine, then call 1967 if they refuse.

sections.heading: Where Your Ration Card Unlocks Other Benefits

items.title: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
items.sub: AAY and PHH households are typically eligible for ₹5 lakh cover. Check at pmjay.gov.in using your card number.

items.title: PM Awas Yojana
items.sub: Used for beneficiary identification and family composition during housing scheme verification.

items.title: RTE school admission
items.sub: Schools accept it as proof of family income and composition for reserved quota seats.

items.title: Address and family proof
items.sub: Accepted for Aadhaar updates, bank accounts, SIM cards and passport applications.

items.title: Scholarships and state schemes
items.sub: Many state welfare applications ask for the card as the income and household reference.

sections.heading: Complaints: Where to Go When the Shop Says No
content: The national NFSA helpline is 1967, and every state runs its own toll-free line alongside it. Complaints can also be filed through the grievance section on nfsa.gov.in.
Report dealers who demand cash for free grain, give short weight, refuse ONORC collection, or claim stock is unavailable without showing the register.
For application delays, most states run Public Service Guarantee Acts with a defined issue timeline. Beyond that, escalate to the District Supply Officer or the state food commission.
Note the date, shop name and what happened before you call. Complaints with specifics get resolved; vague ones get closed.

State helplines run alongside 1967: UP 1800-180-0150, Bihar 1800-3456-194, Delhi 1800-110-841, Maharashtra 1800-222-950, Tamil Nadu 1800-425-5901. Numbers change occasionally, so cross-check on your state food portal.

sections.title: Free grain is guaranteed till December
sections.desc: The Cabinet extended PMGKAY for five years from January 2024. Until then, no NFSA cardholder should pay for their monthly wheat or rice.

sections.heading: The Annual Check Worth Ten Minutes
content: Once a year, open your record on nfsa.gov.in or your state portal and read it properly. Confirm every member is listed, everyone shows verified, the address is current and the category is right.
Also confirm you are actually collecting each month. Several states delete cards that go uncollected for six months or more, and restoration is slower than prevention.
An outdated card quietly costs more than grain. It affects PM-JAY eligibility, housing scheme verification and school admissions that all read the same record.

Do it in March if you want a fixed habit, since that is when many states run verification drives and finish their financial-year cleanups. Catching a problem then means fixing it before the next drive flags you.

sections.text: The grain is free till 2028. The only thing standing between your family and it is an e-KYC nobody told you about.

sections.heading: Migrants: Getting This Right Before You Move
content: Do not surrender or cancel your home-state card when you move for work. Under ONORC that card is what gives you grain in the new city, and cancelling it leaves you with nothing until a fresh application clears.
Complete e-KYC for every member before leaving, including those staying behind, because an unauthenticated member is paused regardless of who is where.
Install Mera Ration 2.0 before travelling and use it to find shops near your new workplace. Collection can be split: family at home draws their share there while you draw yours where you are.
Only apply for a new card in the destination state if you have genuinely relocated permanently, and remove yourself from the old card first to avoid a duplicate flag.
One more practical point: keep a photo of the card and the member list on your phone. Dealers occasionally ask for the physical card, and a clear image plus Aadhaar usually settles it.

faqs.question: I lost my ration card. Can I get a duplicate?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Go to your fair price shop or state food department office with: identity proof (Aadhaar), address proof.

File an application for duplicate card. Processing takes 10-20 days.

In the meantime, you can buy grains using Aadhaar biometric even without the physical card (if ONORC system in your area is active).

faqs.question: My ration card income limit is for BPL but my income actually increased to APL. What do I do?
faqs.answer:
Update your annual income on the food portal or inform your fair price shop. They'll reclassify your card from BPL to APL.

Your monthly grain quota may decrease (APL gets less subsidy). This is actually beneficial - it shows honesty and keeps you compliant with regulations.

faqs.question: Can I transfer my ration card from one state to another?
faqs.answer:
You cannot 'transfer' your card in the traditional sense. However, under ONORC, you can use your existing card in any state by presenting Aadhaar biometric.

If you're permanently moving and want a new card in the new state, apply for new card in that state and surrender old card (or it auto-cancels after 1-2 years of non-use).

faqs.question: My ration card shows me, but my spouse and children are not listed. How do I add them?
faqs.answer:
Go to your state's food portal or fair price shop → 'Add Member to Ration Card'. Provide spouse's name, children's names, their Aadhaar numbers, birth certificates (for children).

Family head's consent is needed. Processing: 7-15 days.

Once approved, their names appear on the card and they become eligible for grains.

faqs.question: Is Aadhaar mandatory for ration card? My elderly parents don't have Aadhaar.
faqs.answer:
Yes, Aadhaar linking is mandatory for all members to receive grains from fair price shops. However, if you or your parents don't have Aadhaar, apply for Aadhaar first (free, same-day in many areas).

Once Aadhaar is issued, link with ration card. Most elderly are able to get Aadhaar; it's free and available for all resident Indians.

faqs.question: The fair price shop says my Aadhaar biometric doesn't match. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Biometric mismatch can happen due to: (1) Your Aadhaar fingerprints not registered properly, (2) Quality issues with shop's biometric reader (dirt, poor maintenance), (3) Your fingerprints have changed (age, injury, heavy work). Try: (1) Wipe your fingers and try again, (2) Try a different finger, (3) Visit another fair price shop to test, (4) Update your Aadhaar biometric at an UIDAI center.

If issue persists, inform the food department.

faqs.question: Can one person hold two ration cards (e.g., from two states)?
faqs.answer:
Technically no, but it can happen if you apply in two states separately and they don't detect the duplicate. Holding two cards is against regulations.

If discovered, both cards are cancelled. Best practice: Hold one card in your state of residence, use ONORC to buy grains elsewhere if migrating.

faqs.question: Ration card e-KYC kaise kare?
faqs.answer:
Teen tarike hain, teenon free. Ration shop par har member ka fingerprint ePoS machine par de dein, ya Mera eKYC app se ghar baithe face scan karein, ya apne state ke PDS portal par OTP se karein.

Har member ka e-KYC zaroori hai, sirf mukhiya ka nahi. Jinka nahi hua unka anaj rok diya jata hai jab tak verification pura na ho.

faqs.question: Is ration free in 2026?
faqs.answer:
Yes, for NFSA cardholders. Under PMGKAY, PHH households get 5 kg per person per month and AAY households get 35 kg per family, at no cost, extended till 31 December 2028.

If a dealer asks for money for this grain, that is illegal. Report it on 1967 or through the grievance section of nfsa.gov.in.

faqs.question: What is the last date for ration card e-KYC?
faqs.answer:
There is no single national date. Each state sets its own deadline for its verification drive, so the only date that applies to you is your state's.

Assam's drive ran to 31 July 2026 and Maharashtra's to 30 June 2026, as examples. Confirm yours at your Fair Price Shop or state food department portal rather than trusting forwarded messages.

faqs.question: How do I check my name in the ration card list?
faqs.answer:
Open nfsa.gov.in, go to ration card details for your state, and search using the card number or any member's Aadhaar. The record shows every listed member with their verification status.

The Mera Ration 2.0 app shows the same member list on your phone. If a name is missing, apply for member addition on your state portal with that person's Aadhaar and relationship proof.

faqs.question: What is Mera Ration 2.0 app used for?
faqs.answer:
It shows your digital ration card with QR code, member list, monthly entitlement and past collections. For migrants it also finds nearby Fair Price Shops and confirms ONORC eligibility.

Several states let you download the e-ration card from the app or DigiLocker as printed cards get phased out.

disclaimer: Ration card processes, NFSA rules, and state-specific procedures may change. This guide is based on information as of March 2026. Always verify current details with your state's food department or official portal.
